205-### Version 292.0
148:- Signed-in account label (v92.0, `claude auth status` in v112.0, WSL support in v113.0): `GetSignedInClaudeAccountLabel()` (NativeChat.cs) is the only synchronous, file-based source in the codebase for *which* Claude account is authenticated — the headless `system/init` event has no account/email field, so it reads `~/.claude.json`'s `oauthAccount.{displayName,emailAddress}` directly, the same state file the CLI itself owns. Best-effort (file is tens of KB, read is negligible next to the rest of a relaunch): any read/parse failure, including racing a CLI write, just returns null and callers show nothing. `BuildWelcomeFacts` still uses it for the passive "Signed in as ..." welcome-screen fact for the Windows provider, where a blocking CLI spawn on every session start would be a bad trade. `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync`'s `appendAccountLabel` path (only set by the Change Account handler) instead calls the async `GetClaudeAuthStatusEmailAsync(isWsl, ...)`, which shells `<resolved claude exe> auth status --json` (or `wsl.exe bash -lic "claude auth status --json"` for WSL) and falls back to the file-based label only if that subprocess call fails — a subprocess round-trip is negligible right after a full process relaunch, and it reads the same authoritative source the CLI itself just updated via `auth login`, rather than the undocumented json field. WSL path (v113.0): `GetSignedInClaudeAccountLabelAsync(isWsl)`/`InvalidateSignedInClaudeAccountLabelAsync(isWsl)` are the WSL-aware overloads — for `ClaudeCodeWSL` they resolve the distro's `$HOME/.claude.json` to its `\\wsl.localhost\` UNC form via `ResolveWslPathAsync` (a `wsl bash -lic "wslpath -w ..."` round-trip, the same approach `ResolveWslSessionDirectoryAsync` in `ClaudeCodeControl.SessionHistory.cs` uses for the transcripts directory) and then read/edit that file exactly like the Windows one. Because that round-trip can't run synchronously on the UI thread, `BuildWelcomeFacts` reads a `_wslAccountLabels` cache instead (keyed by provider, parallel to `_cliVersions`) and `BeginAccountLabelLookup` — mirroring `BeginCliVersionLookup` — fills it in the background and redraws the welcome card via `ShowChatWelcome` once the label is known, which is also what makes a brand-new WSL chat's welcome card show the signed-in account instead of staying silent forever (it previously read the Windows file for a WSL session, so unless the same account happened to be signed in on both sides, the label was always missing). Unlike `_cliVersions`, an empty result is never cached (fixed v113.0): every writer of `_wslAccountLabels` (`BeginAccountLabelLookup`, the resumed-transcript replay, and `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync`'s `appendAccountLabel` path) originally wrote `account ?? string.Empty` unconditionally, following the `_cliVersions` "ask once" convention — correct there because a CLI version genuinely cannot change mid-session, wrong here because "not signed in" routinely flips to "signed in" moments later (mid-login, or a slow write to the CLI's own state file after `auth login` returns). Caching a miss meant `BeginAccountLabelLookup`'s `_wslAccountLabels.ContainsKey(provider)` guard treated that miss as a permanent answer, so once any lookup raced a login that hadn't landed on disk yet, no later welcome card — including a brand-new chat — would ever probe again until the next explicit Change Account click. All three writers now skip the dictionary write entirely when the result is empty, leaving the key absent so the next render's `BeginAccountLabelLookup` retries
389:- Rename / custom titles (v35.0, issue #95): a custom title can be set via the Rename button, the list's right-click context menu, or F2. `ShowRenameSessionDialog()` is a small themed input box prefilled with the current title; an empty result clears the override. Titles persist in `_settings.SessionCustomTitles` (`Dictionary<string,string>` keyed by session UUID, case-insensitive), saved via `SaveSettings()`. `LoadSessionsAsync()` populates `SessionInfo.CustomTitle` from that dict after parsing. A named row shows the name in semibold; the first prompt moves to the tooltip (the green accent bar and `✎` marker were dropped in v276.0, when most rows became named). Deleting a session also removes its title entry. CLI sync (v198.0, issue #170): for Claude Code sessions (native + WSL) a rename also appends the pair Claude Code writes itself for `--name` / an in-CLI rename — `{"type":"custom-title","customTitle":…,"sessionId":…}` + `{"type":"agent-name","agentName":…,"sessionId":…}` — to the transcript (`AppendClaudeTitleRecords`, `BuildClaudeTitleRecords`), which its `/resume` picker and terminal title read (last pair wins; measured on CLI 2.1.280, which itself re-appends the pair on resume). Append-only, `FileShare.ReadWrite`, so a live session writing the file is unaffected; best-effort, failures only hit `Debug.WriteLine`. Clearing a title appends empty strings — NOT verified against the picker. The append bumps the file mtime, but the list date (Session History and the welcome card's recent list) is the last user/assistant record's `timestamp` (`ReadTranscriptRecordTime`), so renaming no longer moves a session to the top and conversations no longer all show the time of the last entrypoint patch or title append. Two call sites: the dialog's rename and the native chat tab's ✎ button (`OnComposerRenameSessionRequested` → `SyncClaudeSessionTitleAsync`, which finds the transcript by session id — workspace project folder first, then any project folder for the Windows store). The first v198.0 build only covered the dialog, so a tab rename wrote nothing. Codex is not synced (App Server owns its metadata)
394:- Resume target (v276.0, native mode only): every resume from the dialog (Resume, double-click) goes through `ChooseHistoryResumeTarget` → `ResumeFromHistoryAsync`. A conversation a chat tab already shows (`TryFindOpenChatTab`, the same check as the welcome card) is only brought forward (`SwitchToOpenChatTabAsync`) — resuming it again left two CLIs writing one transcript. When the tab the dialog was opened from has a user prompt in its transcript (`ChatTabHasConversation`), `AskResumeInNewTab` asks New Tab (default button) / This Tab / Cancel; the question is asked with the history dialog as owner, so Cancel returns to the list. New Tab = `ResumeSessionInNewTabAsync` → `OpenResumedChatTabAsync` (ChatTabRestore.cs, the path that reopens tabs with the solution: deferred launch + transcript replay), seeded with the asking tab's model/effort/permission choices only when it runs the same agent, and carrying its `WorkspaceOverride`. This Tab keeps the old in-place `ResumeSessionAsync`. A tab with no user prompt resumes in place without asking, unless its composer holds a draft (`ChatTabHasDraft`: text, or attachments — `AttachedFiles` for a parallel tab, `attachedImagePaths` for the main chat): then it goes straight to New Tab, since a draft is usually a new topic and resuming over it hid what the user was writing. Terminal mode always resumes in place. Rows of conversations already open end with "· already open"
561:- Live switch: `Apply` raises `Loc.LanguageChanged`. `{local:Loc}` on a dependency property (templates and setters included) is a OneWay binding to the `LocSource` singleton, whose `Language` change re-runs `Loc.L` of the key — WPF listens weakly, so closed chats are not kept alive; elsewhere it stays the text translated at build time. Code that assigns such a property later replaces the binding and owns the text, so `RefreshChatLanguage()` (Settings dialog apply, settings backup load) redoes everything built in code — for the panel: `RefreshToolbarLayout()` (detach caption + the promoted buttons' tooltips, which the chat composers copy as plain text), the working-directory header, effort label, usage-bar labels/stale notice and last-prompt hint; then for the panel chat and every parallel session: `ChatTranscriptView.RefreshLanguage()` (placeholder, clear-button tooltip, modern Stop label, status/activity line, usage popup age, pending interaction cards via PropertyChanged), `UpdateChatComposerState` (selector captions, effort slider, usage ring), the welcome card while it is up, and the tab captions. Stored plain-text captions go through `Loc.Retranslate(shown)` — reverse map of the previous language's strings (first key wins on shared translations), then `L()` in the new one; formatted text is left as is until its next update. The modern/classic floating-button swap saves and restores the buttons' `Content` with `ReadLocalValue`/`RestoreLocalValue` so the binding survives. Messages already in the transcript (history, notices, resolved cards' outcome) keep the language they were written in. Live preview (v270.0): picking a language in the Settings combo calls `PreviewChatLanguage` at once — `Loc.SetLanguage` + `RefreshChatLanguage()` + `LocTree.Retranslate(dialog)` — so the panel, chats, tool windows and the dialog itself switch before OK; OK saves it, Cancel re-applies the saved language (`ApplyChatLanguage` + `RefreshChatLanguage`). `LocTree.Retranslate(root)` (LocExtension.cs) walks the logical tree of a window built in code and passes the window title, TextBlock/Run text and string Content/Header/ToolTip through `Loc.Retranslate`, skipping text boxes (user input) and data-bound properties (a local value would kill the `{local:Loc}` binding); ToolTips and ContextMenus are not logical children, so they are visited explicitly; formatted captions stay until the window is rebuilt. `RefreshChatLanguage()` also uses it for an open GitHub Issues window and redraws the attachment chips. `Loc.Apply` raises `LanguageChanged` listener by listener in try/catch, so one failing window cannot leave the rest in the old language (a throw used to escape into `ApplyChatLanguage`, whose catch fell back to English).
